question: Does the official April 2026 northern Palawan field report support release-ready fish occurrences for Lake Manguao, local streams or estuaries?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Nagao Natural Environment Foundation, Maeda research team. (2026-04-30). Report on survey on Palawan, Philippines. Official project report.
sourcesReviewed.access: Full seven-page English/Japanese report and official project update page reviewed. The report states sampling ran April 10–19, 2026, in northern Palawan.

reportedScope.surveyDesign: The authors explicitly describe the survey as short and non-comprehensive, using several representative locations to glimpse northern Palawan fish fauna.
waterbodiesAndHabitats: Northern Palawan streams, including one surveyed stream with a series of waterfalls

sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.evidence: Specimens were collected from Lake Manguao and northern Palawan streams; the team estimates that the material includes at least two species and says taxonomy will be reviewed in future work.
sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.precision: Genus-level research material; no named species, site coordinates, individual specimen identifiers or accession crosswalk.

sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.evidence: A caption describes two species in Lake Manguao that use different depths; the body text says the lake has multiple endemic cyprinids.
sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.precision: No binomials or specimen identifiers in this report.

sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.evidence: The report says these groups were collected in a mangrove-associated estuary.
sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.precision: No species names, exact estuary name, coordinates or collection accessions.

sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.evidence: The report says the team found this Palawan catfish and describes it as rare/endangered/endemic.
sourceReportedTaxaOrGroups.precision: No named waterbody, station, date-specific specimen code, or collection-vs-market crosswalk. The same report says one team member primarily sourced market specimens; do not assign this name to Lake Manguao or a river. The conservation-status wording remains the report's claim and was not independently verified here.

reportedScope.negativeObservationLimit: Sicydiine gobies were not found in the single waterfall stream surveyed. The authors explicitly note only one stream was checked; this is not evidence of absence elsewhere in northern Palawan.

limits: No complete station register, lat/long, named stream/estuary crosswalk, specimen catalogue number, or machine-readable taxon-by-site table is published in the report.
At least two Boroda species are a provisional estimate pending future taxonomy, not species-level identifications.
Two Barbodes species are pictured/reported without names and cannot be joined to historical lake taxa from appearance, genus or island-level location alone.
The report includes fish collection, market sampling, site observations and broad habitat statements; these evidence types must remain distinct.
The report is not comprehensive and does not inventory all Palawan lakes, rivers, streams, estuaries, catchments or marine habitats.
No item-specific reuse license was identified; no PDF material, image, table, map or underlying data were copied.

crossSourceAssessment.luzonToPalawan: This report extends the same Foundation research program from Luzon into northern Palawan and explicitly adds Lake Manguao, streams and estuarine habitat. Project continuity is not independent replication.
crossSourceAssessment.freshwaterPriority: Lake Manguao is a strong next candidate for targeted review because the official survey names the lake, collected Boroda material there, and refers to unnamed Barbodes species and endemism. Historical studies and collection records are needed to resolve identities and dates.
crossSourceAssessment.coverageMeaning: The report adds freshwater-lake, waterfall-stream and mangrove-estuary leads to the national source inventory; it does not close MIMAROPA or Palawan coverage.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research leads only. No current distribution, abundance, diet, catchability, safety, fishing access, protected boundary, or verified occurrence geometry is approved.

rightsReview.status: No item-specific reuse license was identified for the report during this review.
rightsReview.handling: No PDF, photo, image, table, map or specimen dataset retained. Only source metadata and short factual notes are recorded.

disposition.reason: The report offers important lake, stream and estuary leads but explicitly is non-comprehensive and lacks named species for key groups, precise stations, specimen crosswalks and item-specific reuse terms.

nextAction: Use Lake Manguao as the next focused freshwater batch: retrieve and review the open-access northern Palawan Puntius thesis and accessible institutional metadata for the Lake Manguao fish studies; crosswalk historical binomials to current taxonomic authorities without treating that as specimen re-identification. The SEAFDEC/AQD repository says its 2005 conference paper PDF is unavailable while the publication remains for sale; do not register/login, request a copy or pay without an explicit future decision. Seek vouchers, station/sample data and reuse terms before any app rows.

sources.supports: Full official seven-page northern Palawan survey report, field dates, explicit non-comprehensive limitation, Lake Manguao and stream/station descriptions, genus/group sample statements and source-named taxa.
Official project update page linking the April 2026 Palawan report and giving field-period/location summary.

Official SEAFDEC/AQD repository metadata and abstract for Matillano's 2005 Lake Manguao ichthyofauna paper; page states the PDF is unavailable while the publication remains available in print and for sale. This establishes a follow-up source lead and access limitation, not full-text review.
